title: Trust in Uncertain Times and Deathbed Regret List
author: Ferraro, Roberto
summary: A curated digest highlighting trust rebuilding in uncertain organizational times (replacing assumptions with curiosity), the psychological power of deathbed regrets, and the importance of small consistent actions over grand gestures. Also covers willingness to look stupid as a creative advantage and the difference between productive individuals and productive organizations.
points: Trust is rebuilt through small, consistent daily actions and presence, not grand declarations.
Affective trust (feeling safe) is at higher risk than competence trust in hybrid, restructured organizations.
Willingness to look stupid is a genuine competitive moat in creative and innovative work.
Productive individuals do not automatically make productive organizations or teams.
Reflection on regrets is a powerful tool for clarifying what actually matters in life and work.
quotes: Trust is rebuilt little by little with small day-to-day interactions.
Instead of denying difficulties, face them with presence and small, consistent actions.
Willingness to look stupid is a genuine moat in creative work
Productive individuals don't make productive firms” Archived from Roberto Ferraro Digest on May 2, 2026 by Tim.
